messages.author: bfff38f803dac289
messages.subject: seasonal model: standard deviation of the seasonal random effects
parts:
Hi,

I fitted a spatiotemporal (bym + seasonal) model with four years of disease data (2016-2019) to investigate the factors associated with and predict seasonal disease incidence.

Then, I used this model to predict seasonal incidences for the years 2020 and 2021. It seems that the prediction uses the mean of the spatial and seasonal random effects from 2019. However, the standard deviation of the seasonal effects of 2020 and 2021 increased a lot compared to the standard deviation of those seasonal effects from 2016-2019 (about 6 to 11 times higher for 2020 and 2021, respectively). See the figure below.

Can you please tell me why the model is doing this?  It seems to produce a large variability in the predicted incidence.

Thank you very much for your time and your help!

Regards,

Wen

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] seasonal model: standard deviation of the seasonal random effects
parts:
the behaviour looks kind of ok to me.

its all about how regular each season is... you can test it out with
this code

slen <- 4
n <- 4*10
eta <- sin(2*pi * 1:n/(slen+0.2))
s <- 0.2
y <- eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)
y[n:(n-2*slen)] <- NA
r = inla(y ~ -1 + f(idx,
model = "seasonal",
scale.model=TRUE,
season.length = slen),
data = data.frame(y, idx = 1:n),
control.family = list(hyper = list(prec = list(
initial = log(1/s^2),
fixed = TRUE))))
plot(r)
